# AI Factory Sizer — Blackwell / SuperPOD

> Two tools at penguinai.dugganusa.com. A **generic sizer** that turns a GPU target into a
> defensible bill of materials, and a **cabling breakout** that turns a standardized
> deployment into an install drawing. Sizing-grade: estimates to inform a conversation, not
> a quote, not an electrical or mechanical stamp. Confidence is capped at 95% throughout.

## What each tool is for

- **/index.html — the sizer. Generic.** Any GPU count, any supported architecture, any rack
  feed. Produces nodes, racks, PDUs, fabric, cables and the management plane, plus a SKU
  request sheet. Nodes per rack is `min(space, power)` and which one bound it is reported.
- **/cable.html — the install map. Standardized deployments only.** Takes a published
  reference architecture and breaks out the physical detail the sizer summarises: which U,
  which side, which fault zone, which bundle, which connector. Exports an SVG for install
  teams and an XLS workbook for procurement.

The two are complementary, not alternatives. The sizer answers *what do I buy*. The install
map answers *where does it go, where does it plug in, and what lands where*.

## The rule that governs every number

Every figure is either **read from a vendor** or **computed by us**, and the distinction
travels with the figure rather than living in a footnote. `archSpec().provenance` is
`vendor` or `derived` and rides on downstream values; basis strings say `DERIVED (OURS)` in
words; rule V1 fails the build if a BOM line cites an NVIDIA reference-architecture table on
a fabric computed locally.

Where a vendor publishes no reference architecture, the build is sized **on racks** rather
than on an invented scalable unit, and every derived figure is badged as ours.

## Install map — what is published and what is ours

Published: U-heights, tray counts, port topology, switch models, link counts per scalable
unit, regional rack input connectors.

Ours: A/B side mapping per rack, fault-zone assignment and the loss analysis, riser distance,
slack policy, service loops. **No vendor publishes which way round your PDUs go** — that is a
property of the hall, not the rack.

## The analysis that distinguishes it

Dual-corded equipment is redundant only if its two cords land in two things that cannot fail
together. The map runs one check: **lose any single fault zone — does every rack still have
power, and does the surviving feed stay within its breaker at 80% continuous?** Single-corded
equipment in a lost zone is reported as dropped. A rack at 60% per feed passes every
steady-state drawing and browns out when its partner zone drops.

Per-phase amps = kW × 1000 ÷ (V × √3 × PF). Feed pairs per rack is a control, not a constant:
one pair suits a 5–10 kW enterprise rack and is wrong for a 132 kW GPU rack.

## Reference architectures currently modelled

- **NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 — SpectrumX Enterprise RA.** Per scalable unit (18 trays, 72 GPUs):
  144× 400G compute across dual planes and 4 rails per plane, 36× 400G converged from one
  BlueField-3 B3240 DPU per tray. The compute fabric is **Ethernet (RoCE), not InfiniBand** —
  SN5600 leaves, SN5610 spines. Quantum-X InfiniBand is a different reference architecture.
  Known gap: management is modelled at one run per tray against the document's 71× 1G per SU,
  so that count is a floor rather than a total.
- **Penguin Relion / Altus HGX B300.** The same NVIDIA HGX silicon in an 8U node.

## Cable length method

Device-to-manager allowance at both ends, rise to the pathway, horizontal run at the cabinet
pitch, a service loop each end, a slack factor, rounded up to a stocked length. 1U = 44.45 mm.
Both tools share one ladder so they cannot quote different parts for the same run. Beyond the
ladder the answer is "custom trunk — specify". **Media reach is modelled in the sizer only**,
deliberately in one place.

## What these tools are not

Not a quote. Not an electrical or mechanical stamp. Not a substitute for the as-built
drawing, your local code, or the people who will actually pull the cable. Walk the route
before ordering in volume.
